doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

chapter: Family and early playing in Springfield
title: Hitchhiking home from Max Roach at the Music Barn
summary: He went to Lenox to hear Max Roach, hitchhiked home in the dark, and learned how Max actually played the drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. No mind of my own. Totally susceptible to really out stuff. But I was. And then after that I was on a quest. I knew I had to leave Springfield and go to New York. Around that same time was when Clifford Brown and Richie Powell died. And I had gotten tickets to go to The Music — well it was in Lenox, Massachusetts — The Music Barn. And they used to have these great festivals. But it was way out in the boondocks, it was like you had to take a bus and all that stuff. Anyhow Max was playing there and then I didn’t know that Clifford had died, and I got up there and instead of Clifford they had Kenny Dorham and Sonny Rollins, which they were very killing too.

And I’ll never forget, my bus left at 11:30 and it was fifty miles from Springfield. Now I had to either leave in the middle of the set and miss the last part of it, or hitchhike in the dark home. And I hitchhiked in the dark home. I did. It was cold and I’ll never forget that. It was totally worth it.

I did. I’d heard Max on the records and I’m trying to do his stuff by just listening to it, and of course I had it all wrong. And after I got to see him I could see how he was really doing stuff like [scats] you know there was a way that Max hits each drum, and you couldn’t tell it from just listening like we did in those days. I did a lot of listening.
